segments.text: Twenty-eight million Brazilians don't use the internet. More than eight million can't read. Yet the country's social benefits are explained on websites and apps.
Liga pra Mim, which means Call for Me, is a phone line. You call, you talk, and an AI assistant explains which benefits your family may be entitled to, where to go, and what to bring.
The same assistant also answers on the web, by voice or text. It asks one question at a time, never asks for ID numbers, and never promises approval.

Under the hood, Amazon Connect and Lex handle the call. A Lambda function talks to Claude on Amazon Bedrock, and the model calls two tools: a calculator with the official 2026 rules, and the government's list of eight thousand six hundred social assistance centers.
We tested it with twenty-five real conversations in Portuguese and English. It passed all twenty-five. And if the AI ever goes down, an essential mode keeps the line answering.
Built from zero with Claude Code, by someone who had never used AWS before. Because a right you can't find is a right you don't have.
